review_basis: Visually inspected all 23 original numbered Module 11 WebP slides directly, including the actual titles, diagrams, labels, examples and cautions; source order and concept boundaries were verified before narration.

scenes.title: Data Governance Strategies
scenes.narration: Begin at the data council on the left. A cross-functional group defines standards, permitted uses and difficult trade-offs. The next column distinguishes three roles: the data owner approves purposes and access, the data steward maintains metadata and quality, and the data custodian operates storage, security and backups. These are responsibilities, not necessarily three separate employees. Step three governs sharing through agreements specifying allowed uses, Lake Formation for supported data permissions, IAM for AWS access and S3 for storage and encryption. Step four monitors how the data is used and trains practitioners in responsible handling. The bottom example follows internal documents for a generative AI application: council approval, owner authorization, steward preparation, custodian protection and monitored use by practitioners. The desired outcome is trustworthy data and clear accountability, not simply making every document accessible to a model.

scenes.title: Data Management Concepts
scenes.narration: Read this five-stage lifecycle from left to right: collection, processing, storage, consumption, then archive or deletion. For collection, the slide lists Kinesis for streaming events, IoT Core for device data and DataSync for moving files. Processing examples include AWS Glue for preparation, EMR for large-scale processing and Lambda for event-driven operations. Storage choices include S3 objects, RDS relational records and DynamoDB NoSQL items. Consumption may involve QuickSight dashboards, SageMaker models or Athena querying data in S3. Long-term archives can use suitable S3 storage classes, while data no longer needed may be deleted. The row beneath adds logging, Region or data-residency choices, monitoring, analysis and retention policy across all stages. Follow the application-log example at the bottom. Most importantly, the slide states there is no universal fixed retention period: business needs, contracts and applicable law decide how long records must be kept.

scenes.title: Data Lineage
scenes.narration: Data lineage means being able to trace a result back through the data and operations that produced it. Follow the five boxes. First, preserve source metadata such as the data's owner, collection time and license in S3. Second, record each cleaning or transformation step and its version; the diagram shows versions one, two and three, with Glue as an example preparation service. Third, preserve the exact version of the training dataset. Fourth, associate the resulting SageMaker model artifact with its training data, code, parameters, creator and time. Fifth, for a prediction, record the input reference, model version, preprocessing and timestamp, with suitable logs such as CloudWatch. The product-review example shows a positive sentiment prediction. With lineage, an analyst can investigate whether it came from the original licensed review data, the current cleaning process and the correct model version. That supports reproducibility, auditability and responsible debugging.
